# Contract: systematic-debugging

Third-party skill from [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) (MIT, Jesse Vincent), skills-bundle snapshot 2026-11-13. SumitCraft set the folder name and the description so the skill fills one gap (A root-cause debugging procedure before any fix). The method is upstream. Category: engineering. Kind: guidance-only (no scripts by design).

## Purpose
Find the root cause of a bug or a failing test before proposing a fix.

## Use it for
- "this is broken and I do not know why"
- "debug this failure before changing code"

## Not for
- which commit introduced it (bisect-anything)
- a test that fails only sometimes (flaky-test-killer)

## Accepted inputs
A failure: error output, a test, or a behaviour that does not match expectations.

## Deliverables
A root-cause account, then a fix that follows from it.

## Prerequisites
Required:
- none

Optional:
- Python 3.9+

Check them with `node tools/doctor.mjs` (Windows: `tools\doctor.ps1`).

## Local and network behaviour
Local only.

## Cost-sensitive operations
None.

## Workflow
1. Read Error Messages Carefully
2. Reproduce Consistently
3. Check Recent Changes
4. Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems
5. Trace Data Flow
6. Find Working Examples
7. Compare Against References
8. Identify Differences
9. Understand Dependencies
10. Form Single Hypothesis
11. Test Minimally
12. Verify Before Continuing
13. When You Don't Know
14. Create Failing Test Case
15. Implement Single Fix
16. Verify Fix
17. If Fix Doesn't Work
18. If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture

Full steps: [SKILL.md](SKILL.md).

## Human decisions
- What counts as the failing behaviour

## Quality checks
- No fix is proposed before the cause is identified
- The failing case is re-run after the change

## Common failures
- A symptom patch with the cause still unknown
